findings.F1: The confirmed 28-day momentum rests mostly on one coin. Coin by coin, the t of the 10-day unusual return on the 28-day return is 2.86 for ZEC and between -0.95 and 1.26 for the other five (about 210 grid cases each). Pooled over both sides, the 28-day return reaches only t 1.66 on 1259 cases.
findings.F2: The fall side carries nothing, which supports refusing shorts. On the 615 grid cases with a 28-day fall, the slope of the 10-day unusual move on the size of the fall has t 0.21, and their mean strength is -0.032 (t -0.88).
findings.F3: Large one-day falls are followed by rebounds; large one-day rises are not followed by declines. On a non-overlapping 3-day grid, the 288 days whose return was below -1.5 standard deviations were followed by a 3-day unusual move of +0.169 of the coin's usual 3-day move. The 286 days above +1.5 were followed by -0.018. The slope on the size of these large days has t -1.96, and over all 5435 cases the one-day return predicts the next 3 days with t -2.44.
findings.F4: Inside the rise side, the 28-day rise is graded only when volatility is low. In the lowest 20-day-volatility tercile the slope has t 2.30 (215 cases); in the middle and high terciles it is -0.31 and -0.11 (212 and 217 cases). The mean 10-day strength is still 0.002 in the low tercile against 0.063 in the other two.
findings.F5: The 5-day return adds to the 28-day return over 10 days (t 3.70 for the 5-day return given the 28-day one, t 0.03 the other way round, 1547 cases), but it does not hold up. It fades at 5 days (t 0.14), appears mostly in windows w13 to w24 (t 2.43 against 0.83 in w1 to w12), and mostly in ZEC (t 3.84 against -0.32 to 1.34 elsewhere). With this many angles tested, I do not count it as standing out.
findings.F6: The book's gain comes from rare long trades:
findings.F7: The book's best and worst 5 % of days both come after the coin has risen about 7 % over the 5 days before (+7.4 % before the best, +7.1 % before the worst; 648 days each). They sum to +3.2 and -2.5 times the book's total gain, so the book's result is a narrow difference between its tails.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's fall over its last day, the higher its return over the next 3 days, relative to its normal drift.
ideas.consequence: A trader would lean long after a coin's sharp one-day drop, more the deeper the drop, rather than selling into it.
ideas.name: rebound after sharp daily falls

ideas.idea: While a coin's 20-day volatility is low compared with its own past, the larger its 28-day rise, the higher its return over the next 10 days.
ideas.consequence: A trader would trust a 28-day rise as a reason to go long mainly in calm markets, and refuse to size up on it when volatility is high.
ideas.name: calm-market 28-day momentum
